title: Stackification preserves module sheaves and quasi-coherence
statement: Fix the universe and small-site convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal P$ be a category fibred in groupoids over $S$-schemes: every base map admits a cartesian lift, all arrows are cartesian, and arrows over identities are invertible. Let $q:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P^\#$ be its fppf stackification [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description], for the big fppf topology [def-pc-fppf-site]. On either category the site has its objects and arrows, with covers those lying over fppf covering families; the structure sheaf at an object over $T$ is $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$, with regular-function pullback as restriction [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Module sheaves mean [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; quasi-coherent means locally admitting presentations $\mathcal O^{(I)}\to\mathcal O^{(J)}\to F\to0$ for small sets $I,J$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Precomposition with $q$, with the identical structure rings on corresponding objects, gives an equivalence $q^*:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{\mathcal P^\#})\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{\mathcal P})$, on all module maps, whose value satisfies $(q^*F)(x)=F(qx)$. A module $F$ on $\mathcal P^\#$ is quasi-coherent if and only if $q^*F$ is quasi-coherent. Thus this same functor restricts to an equivalence on the full subcategories of quasi-coherent modules. No algebraicity of either fibred category is assumed.

source.place: Tags 06WQ (lemma-stackification) and 06WR (lemma-stackification-quasi-coherent); q^* is written in its contravariant, precomposition direction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-fibred-site-functor-continuity] to the functor $q$ over $\mathit{Sch}/S$, with its fppf site. Thus both inherited sites are defined, $q$ preserves covering families and their pullbacks, precomposition preserves set sheaves, and $q$ is cocontinuous. In particular any covering of $qx$ lifts, up to isomorphism over $qx$, to a covering of $x$. All total sites and sheaf carriers are taken in the universes fixed in the statement.

source.place: Tag 06WQ, proof: continuity and cocontinuity from Tag 06NW.

proof.text: Check the remaining conditions of [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor]. For $x',x$ and a fixed base map $u:T'\to T$, cartesian lifting identifies arrows $x'\to x$ over $u$ with fibre isomorphisms $x'\cong u^*x$. By [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description], their presheaf maps to its associated isomorphism sheaf. Sheafifying this unit gives an isomorphism by the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; hence [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] says both that an isomorphism in the target lifts locally and that two source isomorphisms with equal images agree locally. These give local fullness and local faithfulness, also for arbitrary arrows over $u$. Finally the local-essential-image clause of the stackification node gives a covering $\{qx_i\to y\}$ of every target object $y$. Together with step 1 these are exactly the five special-cocontinuity conditions.

source.place: Tag 06WQ, proof: conditions (3)-(5) of Sites Tag 03A0 from stackification.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-sheaf-equivalence], restriction $E$ along $q$ is an equivalence on set sheaves. It is also an equivalence on abelian sheaves: use [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-abelian-component] to view these as commutative group objects. Given an abelian sheaf on the source, choose its underlying set sheaf preimage $B$ under $E$. Since $E$ preserves finite products and the terminal object by [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits], full faithfulness lifts its addition, zero and inverse uniquely to $B$. The group identities hold because their images under faithful $E$ hold. The same fullness lifts precisely the morphisms commuting with these operations. This constructs an essentially surjective and fully faithful restriction on abelian sheaves, hence an equivalence by [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence].

source.place: Tag 03A0; algebraic-structure transport as in Sites Section 00YR and Proposition 00YV.

proof.text: For every $x$ over $T$, the rings on $x$ and $qx$ are both $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$, and restrictions are the same pullbacks of functions [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Thus the restricted target ring sheaf is the source ring sheaf, with identity scalar map. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-dense-subsite-module-restriction] now hold: continuity is step 1, the two sheaf equivalences are step 3, and cover-density is step 2. This gives the required module equivalence. Its value and action on module morphisms are precomposition, so $(q^*F)(x)=F(qx)$ and every module morphism is included.

source.place: Tag 06WR, first assertion and equality of the structure sheaves.

proof.text: For $x$ over $T$, identify both slice categories $\mathcal P/x$ and $\mathcal P^\#/qx$ with $(\mathit{Sch}/S)/T$. Indeed, the forgetful functor from either slice sends an arrow into its fixed object to its underlying scheme map into $T$. It is essentially surjective by cartesian lifting. For two such arrows into the fixed object and a commuting base triangle, the target arrow is cartesian, so there is a unique arrow between their domains over that base triangle making the total triangle commute. This proves full faithfulness. By [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence] these are equivalences; since $q$ lies over the identity of the base, $q_x:\mathcal P/x\to\mathcal P^\#/qx$ is therefore an equivalence too. Both slice topologies have coverings exactly over fppf coverings, so $q_x$ preserves and reflects coverings; the restricted rings agree as in step 4.

source.place: Tag 06WR, identification of the restrictions at x and qx as sheaves on the same big fppf scheme site.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-sheaf-transport] to $q_x$: restriction is an equivalence for sets and for abelian groups, and $q_x$ is continuous and cover-dense. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-dense-subsite-module-restriction] applies on these slices. The resulting module equivalence $E_x$ commutes with restriction of global modules, since both expressions on an arrow $z\to x$ are $F(qz)$, with the same restriction maps and scalar action. By [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits], $E_x$ and its inverse preserve coproducts, kernels and cokernels. Additivity follows sectionwise from [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Since $E_x$ sends the restricted structure sheaf to the restricted structure sheaf, it carries $\mathcal O^{(I)}$ to $\mathcal O^{(I)}$ for every small $I$, and preserves and reflects exact presentations by such free modules.

source.place: Tag 03DG, intrinsic global presentations; Tag 03DF, free modules and right exactness of pullback. Here the slice equivalence is the explicit scheme-slice comparison in step 5.

proof.text: Suppose $F$ is quasi-coherent on $\mathcal P^\#$. For every $x$, choose a covering $\{y_a\to qx\}$ on which $F$ has free presentations, as in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Step 1 lifts it to a covering $\{x_a\to x\}$ with $qx_a\cong y_a$ over $qx$. Transfer the chosen presentation first along this isomorphism of objects, then along the slice equivalence $E_{x_a}$ of step 6. Its result is a free presentation of $q^*F$ on $\mathcal P/x_a$. Thus $q^*F$ is quasi-coherent by the same definition.

source.place: Tag 06WR, preservation of quasi-coherence (Tag 06WH); explicit local-presentation argument.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $q^*F$ is quasi-coherent. For an arbitrary $y\in\mathcal P^\#$ choose a covering $\{qx_i\to y\}$ using [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. For each $x_i$ choose a covering $\{x_{ij}\to x_i\}$ and a free presentation of $q^*F$ on $\mathcal P/x_{ij}$ by [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. By reflection in step 6 this is a free presentation of $F$ on $\mathcal P^\#/qx_{ij}$. The families $\{qx_{ij}\to qx_i\}$ cover by step 1, and their composites cover $y$ by transitivity of coverings. Hence $F$ is quasi-coherent. The equivalence in step 4 now restricts to the full quasi-coherent subcategories: it remains fully faithful on their Hom sets, and any quasi-coherent source module has a preimage under the equivalence which is quasi-coherent by the implication just proved. None of these arguments uses algebraicity.

source.place: Tag 06WR, reflection via local essential surjectivity and local presentations; compare Modules on Sites Tag 03DN.

proof_origin.place: Tags 06WQ and 06WR; the scheme-test comparison in the latter is spelled out using cartesian slices and free presentations.
